text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Unusual surge in tool-invoke latency and structured-output serialization failures in eu-central-1. Automatic protective actions suggested: enable schema-lock and api-key circuit-breakers. Paging oncall.

Maya (oncall): picking up. I'm seeing lots of 504s tied to /v1/agent/tool-invoke and a spike in timeouts when clients request full structured JSON. Queue depth for the tool-worker pool doubled in 6m.

Linh (sre): memory and alloc profiles show long-tail allocations from large JSON assembly and repeated retries from some webhook-based integrations. A handful of API keys are making small bursts but with many concurrent tool calls.

Carla (eng): quick hits we can do live: 1) enable api-key level circuit-breakers (trip on error budget or sustained latency) 2) enable schema-lock: only allow compact, pre-approved JSON keys for non-enterprise tenants 3) throttle tool-invoke routes by API key when above threshold.

Priya (oncall-3): recommend we apply three mitigations in this order to limit customer impact: A) per-api-key soft circuit with auto-unfreeze B) switch non-committed tenants to compact-mode responses (plain text + minimal JSON) C) raise 429 backoff headers so clients don't aggressively retry.

deploy-bot: proposing rollout commands:
```
rbctl circuit create --scope api_key --path /v1/agent/tool-invoke --errors 5 --window 60s --cooldown 300s
rbctl feature toggle --name compact_structured_mode --target non_enterprise --state enabled
rbctl traffic set --path /v1/agent/tool-invoke --limit 30r/s
```

Maya (oncall): run those. Also add a temporary schema whitelist on gateway: only keys ["status","result","meta"] allowed for compact_mode.

Carla (eng): gateway patch ready. Applying now. Patch:
```
PATCH /gateway/tenant-config
{
  "compact_structured_whitelist": ["status","result","meta"],
  "force_compact_for_tiers": ["freemium","self-serve"]
}
```

Linh (sre): I'm deploying the circuit-breaker rule. Expecting affected API keys to get short-lived 503/429 responses which should stop retries. Also adding a short-lived metric rule to suppress noisy alerts while we stabilize.

Priya (oncall-3): I'll apply the token-bucket per-api-key limiter for particularly chatty keys. Command:
```
rbctl quotas update --api-key XXXXXX --tool-invoke 10r/s
```
We've identified ~12 keys that are above safe thresholds.

Dave (product): Be mindful: compact_mode removes some structured hooks customers rely on. Emma, prepare a targeted comms blast to any tenants we throttle or put into compact-mode. Make it clear enterprise customers can request an exemption.

Emma (support): drafting messages. Posting to #support-ops and queueing priority tickets for impacted paying customers. Also creating a short status update for status.redwood.ai with link to contact support for exemptions.

Maya (oncall): also add a temporary header 'X-Redwood-Compact: enforced' so clients can detect compact mode and degrade gracefully.

Carla (eng): adding header now via gateway patch. Also adding a debounce to retries by returning 'Retry-After: 8' for throttled requests to discourage tight retry loops.

Linh (sre): early telemetry: within 90s of enabling circuit-breakers and compact mode, average worker RSS dropped ~22%. Error-rate peaked then started trending down. A few enterprise API keys hit the circuit briefly; they were auto-exempted by allowlist rules.

Priya (oncall-3): note for handoff: I'll stay until p95 < 600ms and no new OOMs in the tool-worker pool for 10m. If we see more than 3 enterprise exemptions triggered in 5m, escalate to eng.

deploy-bot: rollout summary: compact_mode enabled for non-enterprise at 1725002485, circuit-breakers deployed at 1725002496, per-api-key quotas applied at 1725002510.

Maya (oncall): support, what are customers seeing?

Emma (support): most customers report degraded structured payloads but services remain functional. A few webhook-based integrations experienced temporary failures; raised tickets with affected teams and sent exemption forms for enterprise.

Carla (eng): pushed an emergency sanitizer that truncates tool outputs >40kb to avoid huge serializations; it's reversible. Also added an instrumentation flag to log serialization time > 30ms for postmortem.

Linh (sre): monitoring for retry storms — added temporary backoff headers and jitter. So far, no signs of thundering herd. Error-rate down to ~1.3%, queue depth steady.

Dave (product): action items: 1) prioritize a follow-up RFC for streaming-first structured serialization 2) evaluate per-tenant tool-invoke billing tie-ins to discourage runaway usage 3) document circuit-breaker behavior for customers.

Maya (oncall): preparing handoff: once 15m of stability achieved I'll hand to Priya. Keep checklist for rollback: - disable compact_mode flag - remove api-key circuit-breakers - restore normal quotas and remove sanitizer

Priya (oncall-3): taking over contingent on 15m stability. I'll keep on-call pager open. If error-rate creeps above 2% for 5m or we see new OOMs, I'll page eng.

incident-bot: MITIGATION LOG: compact_mode enabled (1725002485), api-key circuit-breakers created (1725002496), sanitizer active (1725002520), quotas applied (1725002510). Continue monitoring.

Maya (oncall): handing off now. Final check: p95 480ms, error-rate 1.0%, memory stabilized. Nice rapid coordination everyone. :shipit!
